subject: general
question: Which island was renamed as Swaraj Dweep?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Havelock Island**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Havelock Island, part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, was renamed Swaraj Dweep in **December 2018** by the Government of India.
 
• The renaming was announced by PM Narendra Modi during the **celebration of the 75th anniversary of the hoisting of the Indian flag by Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose** in Port Blair.
 
• The new name, Swaraj Dweep, pays tribute to Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose, who referred to the Andaman Islands as the first Indian territory freed from British rule in 1943.
 
• Havelock Island is one of the most popular tourist destinations in the Andaman Islands, known for its pristine beaches like Radhanagar Beach and Elephant Beach.
 
• The renaming reflects India’s commitment to honor its historical heroes and their contributions to the country’s independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose and Andaman:**

 
 
• Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose hoisted the Indian flag on the Andaman Islands on **30 December 1943**, declaring it free from British rule.
 
• He named the Andaman and Nicobar Islands as Swaraj and Shaheed Dweep, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Renaming of Islands:**
 
 
• In addition to Havelock Island, two other islands were renamed: Ross Island became **Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep**, and Neil Island became **Shaheed Dweep**.
 
• The renaming initiative was part of an effort to align the islands' names with India’s freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Tourism at Swaraj Dweep:**
 
 
• Swaraj Dweep is famous for its crystal-clear waters, coral reefs, and adventure activities like snorkeling and scuba diving.
 
• Radhanagar Beach, located on the island, is often listed among Asia’s best beaches.
 
 
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands:**
 
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a union territory of India, comprising around 572 islands.
 
• They are located at the juncture of the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea.
